title: Hearing tech startup Legato emerges from stealth with $12M and a peek at its AI hearing glasses
slides: Legato's AI hearing glasses—can they truly restore natural hearing?
They emerged with $12M and a glimpse at their technology.
Unlike existing aids, these glasses adapt to each user's auditory profile.
Early users report understanding speech in noisy rooms effortlessly.
Your next hearing aid may quietly disappear into your eyewear.
thread_text:
1. Can AI glasses replace hearing aids?

A startup called Legato just secured $12 million to develop glasses that might make traditional hearing aids obsolete.

2. How do they differ?

They adapt to each user's unique auditory profile, offering a personalized hearing experience that current aids lack.

3. The real-world test

Early users report understanding conversations in noisy environments effortlessly—something standard aids struggle with.

4. Beyond the hype

If these glasses deliver, they could quietly integrate hearing support into everyday eyewear, changing assistive tech forever.

5. What would you do?

Would you swap your hearing aid for glasses that look normal? Try a demo if available—experience the difference yourself.

instagram.caption:
Hearing aids may soon hide inside your glasses. Legato just showed off AI-powered eyewear that adapts to your personal hearing profile—and raised $12M to make it real. Early users say they can finally follow conversations in noisy restaurants, something standard aids often fail at. 👓

The tech maps how you hear and adjusts in real time, instead of applying a one-size-fits-all boost. That could mean ditching the visible earpiece for a frame that looks normal.

For anyone who’s struggled to catch a word at a busy table, this is the upgrade you’ve been waiting for. Would you trade your current device for a pair of glasses that do both? 🔇
